text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- In its statement to parliament today, the government will restate its commitment to promote development, ease the burden on ordinary people, not to raise prices and to find instant solutions to their problems.

- Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak had a telephone conversation with King Fahd of Saudi Arabia yestreday evening on developments in the Middle East and a number of issues of interest to the two countries.

- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri and Oil Minister Hamdi el-Banbi discussed yesterday the results of the new gas discovery in the Western Desert. Banbi said the discovery was by Khalda Petroleum, a joint venture incluing Repsol and Apache. A test well called Tut 1, 65 km (40 miles) southwest of Marsa Matrouh town, found three strata bearing gas and condensate with a total thickness of 50 metres (160 feet).
- Ahmed Khawaga, the head of the Egyptian Bar Association, died yesterday of a heart attack aged almost 70.
- Mubarak has appointed Major-General Hitler Tantawi as chairman of the administrative audit authority.
- Ganzouri lays out the future of development in Egypt when he makes his statement to parliament.
- Mubarak will meet Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai tomorrow, an Israeli defence ministry statement said.

- Transport Minister Soleiman Metwalli said a team from the Egyptian Railways Board will go to Libya at the beginning of next week to discuss technical details of plans to lay 2,000 km (1,200 miles) of track along the coast from the Egyptian-Libyan border, past Benghazi and Tripoli, to the Tunisian border. Under an agreement with Libya, the Egyptian Railways Board will carry out this project.
- Ganzouri said that 1997 will be the year of the private sector and encouraging private investment in new fields, such as airports, power stations and roads.
